name: l27-cloud-gpu-diffs
title: Why a cloud GPU node differs
spec: Four boxes around a centre box 'cloud GPU node': Noisy neighbours (shared CPU caches, memory bandwidth, NIC; shows as %steal and latency outliers); Virtual topology (the NUMA layout and PCIe tree the provider presents; flat view stops NCCL choosing best paths); Passthrough and SR-IOV (whole GPU passed through, NIC as virtual function; provider sets bandwidth caps, MTU, counters); Nested virtualisation (two layers of exits; often disabled on GPU types). Green bar: if a workload is slower in the cloud, check these four before you blame the software.
anchor: ### Why a cloud GPU node behaves differently
alt: Noisy neighbours, virtual topology, passthrough limits and nested virtualisation explain most cloud surprises.
cap: Check these four differences before blaming the software for a slower cloud GPU node.

name: l27-gpu-options
title: Where to run a GPU workload
spec: Table with Option, Pro, Con. Rows: GPU VM with passthrough | provisioning API, snapshots, tenant isolation, near-native GPU | hypervisor overhead on I/O unless offloaded ; Bare-metal instances | full topology and NIC/GPU control, no hypervisor, InfiniBand | longer provisioning, you own more of the stack ; Containers on VMs or bare metal | fast start, reproducibility | shared kernel, visibility limits ; MIG / vGPU slices | many small tenants on one GPU | no NCCL across MIG instances ; MicroVMs/Kata | strong isolation | GPU support complexity. Orange mark on Containers: almost all AI workloads run on top of one of the others.
anchor: ### VM, bare metal or container for GPUs?
alt: Five ways to run GPU workloads compared by their pros and cons.
cap: Each option trades control for convenience, so read the cons column as carefully as the pros.

name: l27-limits-use
title: Software limits under USE
spec: Table with Resource, Utilisation, Saturation. Rows: CPU quota | cpu.stat usage_usec vs cpu.max | nr_throttled, throttled_usec, PSI cpu ; Memory limit | memory.current vs memory.max | memory.events (high, max), PSI memory; errors oom_kill, exit 137 ; Disk I/O limit | io.stat vs io.max | io.pressure, latency growth ; PIDs | pids.current vs pids.max | fork failures, Resource temporarily unavailable ; VM vCPUs | guest CPU utilisation | %steal, run queue. Orange note: utilisation is measured against the limit, not against the physical resource. Names monospace.
anchor: ## 5. Resource controls under the USE method
alt: Each software limit paired with the signals that show whether it is binding.
cap: Utilisation is measured against the limit, not the physical resource, which is what makes the table useful in a shared cloud.
